content:
We got two templates. The first seems relevant: it involves a ketone and an alkyne (C#C) reacting to form a cyclic product with a silyl group. The mapped_rxn shows product is our target? Let's examine product_smiles from first entry: product_smiles = '[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1(/[CH:6]=[CH:7]/[c:8]2[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19]'

That matches our target: methyl ester (COC...), a cyclohexene fused to phenyl, with silyl group. Yes.

Reactant_smiles: 'O=[C:5]([C:3]([O:2][CH3:1])=[O:4])[CH2:6][CH2:7][c:8]1[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]1.[CH:14]#[C:15][Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19]'

So precursors are: a ketone with an aliphatic chain attached to aromatic ring (maybe a phenylpropyl ketone) and a silyl acetylene.

Thus we need to return all possible precursors of applying the template. The template may generate multiple precursor sets if multiple matches. We can apply the template to our target using apply_template with template_id? We need template ID. The result includes reaction_id and template_hash but not ID. Possibly template ID is the reaction_id? Or we can use the retro_smarts_template directly with apply_template? The tool apply_template expects template_id, not SMARTS. We need to retrieve template by ID. Maybe the ID is the reaction_id? Let's try apply_template with template_id = "1914386".
